title: HyperET: Efficient Training in Hyperbolic Space for Multi-modal Large Langu

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The deduction assumes exp_0^{D,c}(W0 X) = exp_0^{D,c}(W0) exp_0^{D,c}(X). The exponential map in hyperbolic space is not an algebra homomorphism, so Y0^{D_c^n} = W0^{D_c^n} X^{D_c^n} and the subsequent radius derivation are mathematically invalid.

Möbius scalar/matrix multiplication is defined only for a point X in D_c^n (a vector) and a matrix M in R^{n×n}. In Eqs. (9)-(10) it is applied to weight matrices W0/exp(W0), and the output of the logarithmic map is then treated as a matrix W multiplying X. No exponential/logarithmic map for matrices is defined, so the operations have mismatched types/dimensions.

For Möbius scalar multiplication, ||s⊗X|| = (1/√c)|tanh(s atanh(√c||X||))|, so Rad_{s⊗X} = |s| Rad_X, not s Rad_X, unless s ≥ 0. The theorem and Eq. (2) omit the required nonnegativity restriction on the learnable scalar s.

The appendix labels the theorem 'Revised Flawed' and states 'this relation does not strictly hold due to nonlinearities... precise control over radius via scalar multiplication is not guaranteed,' while the main text and immediately following text claim precise radius adjustment via Möbius multiplication. This is a direct contradiction and appears to be a leftover revision note.

The paper admits that 'HyperET is trained with an extended schedule and augmented compute budget not matched in the baseline settings. Such discrepancies may contribute significantly to improved results, complicating direct attribution to HyperET alone.' Thus the pre-training comparison is not controlled, and the reported improvements cannot be attributed to HyperET.
The fine-tuning section explicitly omits 'learning rate, weight decay, batch sizes, training steps, and adapter insertion points' and only notes c=0.01, making the experiments irreproducible.

The text says 'The weights of HyperET are implemented with the three scaling matrices and integrated into the model's attention layers,' but Table 1 states 'Ours: we realize the extra learnable parameters as diagonal matrices, i.e., W_s^D.' It is unclear which configuration was actually used in the main fine-tuning experiments.

The paragraph claims 'baseline MemVP generally outperforms HyperET-enhanced LaVIN by a small margin, with inconsistent improvements noted,' but Table 1 shows HyperET improves every corresponding baseline average (LaVIN+Ours vs LaVIN, MemVP+Ours vs MemVP), and comparing MemVP baseline to LaVIN+Ours is not an evaluation of HyperET. It also asserts 'fails to reach the top accuracy of MemVP-LLaMA-13B, contradicting claims of performance parity,' although no parity claim appears and MemVP+Ours-7B actually ties MemVP-13B baseline at 93.78.

The text says 'Results were largely similar regardless of the multiplication operation used. This suggests Möbius multiplication may have limited practical impact,' but Table 5 shows removing ⊗_c lowers scores by about 1.2–1.8 points across VQAv2, GQA, VizWiz, SQA, and TextVQA.
LLaVA-Next is cited as [39], but [39] is the LLaVA-1.5/Improved Baselines paper; the correct LLaVA-NeXT reference is [32].
MME is cited as [67], but reference [67] is Yin et al., 'A survey on multimodal large language models'; the actual MME benchmark paper is not the cited work and is missing from the reference list.

CLIP is cited as [54] (EVA-CLIP), and CLIP's vision encoder is cited as [69,54], where [69] is SigLIP. The original CLIP paper is [50], already in the reference list, so these citations misattribute the CLIP encoder.

The sentence 'Existing hyperbolic space methods often manipulate hierarchical embeddings or impose constraints to improve modality alignment [incorrect ref]' contains a literal '[incorrect ref]' placeholder instead of a real citation.

It defines W_s^{B-D}=diag(R_1,...,R_r) with R_i∈R^{n/r×n/r} and then says 'r is the block size,' but r is the number of blocks and n/r is the block size. The stated degeneration condition r=n (1×1 blocks giving diagonal) confirms this terminology error.

The caption says 'Top-1 accuracy is reported,' but the MME column contains scores such as 1510.7, 1536.2, and 1584.7, which are not top-1 accuracy percentages. MME is a total evaluation score, not an accuracy metric.
Q-Former is introduced by BLIP-2 [35], not by InstructBLIP [16]; citing [16] for 'Q-former' is a misattribution.
